Seeking a way to announce prayer in Medina, Muslims proposed a bell, horn or fire; Bilal was told to call, doubling the Adhan's phrases and saying the Iqama's once.
Bilal and the blind Ibn Umm Maktum called the Adhan; the Prophet attacked at dawn only where he heard none, and said a goatherd calling it had left the Fire.
Those hearing the mu'adhdhin should repeat his words, then bless the Prophet and ask al-Wasila, a rank in Paradise, for him; such responses bring his intercession, forgiveness and Paradise.
At the iqama people were not to stand till they saw the Prophet; once he left the formed rows to bathe, and Bilal said the iqama only on seeing him.
On cold, windy or rainy nights the Prophet had the caller tell people to pray in their dwellings, as Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas did, even on a rainy Friday.
